First reasoned static review: Agent Tesla scripts and bitmap assembly loader

Verdicts
- b003c026b2e1e32e357d66d93ad46b45a5bec3552297d58aa19ae202462a8537:
  MALICIOUS. AES-wrapped Agent Tesla credential stealer with configured FTP
  delivery and a reflected process-injection helper.
- 264f8bdf1282724620ad023ac956fb5263d849e4973d333f03da00dddd8bc111:
  MALICIOUS. The same stealer/injector code with different FTP credentials.
- 6ef0475a2947228b255910ecb1afbfb67d84422890530465af83dd8962b511ea:
  MALICIOUS. SteamLaundry executable runs bitmap-concealed assemblies during
  form construction. Supplied provenance attributes it to Formbook; the
  ultimate payload's family and theft behavior were not independently recovered.

Method and provenance
Ran atomscan in slow mode with updates disabled and cleave facts on each input.
Verified the supplied SHA-256 values and examined PE/CLR headers, resources,
user strings, metadata tokens, IL branches, call arguments and configuration.
Decoded bytes only; did not execute the scripts, assemblies or native images.
Python dnfile/dncil supplied token-resolved IL. Pillow decoded image pixels;
PyCryptodome reproduced AES-CBC/PKCS7 and SmartAssembly resource decryption.
The supplied Bazaar/Triage/VT/MalShare reports corroborate collection context,
but their public pages could not be retrieved in this session. Their labels
and the ensemble scores were not used as proof of payload behavior.
No fetched dependency is involved in these three standalone delivery files.

PowerShell execution chain (both samples)
The visible "PS Secure Loader" strips whitespace from Base64 ciphertext and
embedded key/IV, decrypts AES-CBC with PKCS7 padding, then passes the UTF-8
script to Invoke-Expression. The result defines a five-second process loop.
It tests for aspnet_compiler, Base64-decodes and XOR-unmasks an assembly, loads
that assembly with Reflection.Assembly.Load, resolves FILES.WHORE.LAUNCHER,
and supplies a Framework v4 aspnet_compiler.exe path plus payload bytes.
The helper reads PE headers/sections, creates a suspended host, allocates and
writes its image, updates the thread context and resumes the thread. This is
a hollowing-style execution path. The helper is identical in both scripts:
  SHA-256 3aa22687394040b5f1536937589c23ac08d8642e5d7ad4b7369b938ca600929c
The decimal MZ arrays contain separate unsigned managed executables:
  b003 payload 8e262e02cf774d6be40777abafd8033c5b839314fb6aaa49cde1f4ff03493277
  264f payload 63730a04620bca56f24de059c6b02a375f7d7a86e6cd299b9886a130a74cbf5c
Their token-resolved IL differs only in the embedded FTP username/password.

The scripts assign their decimal payload array after the launch attempt.
The first attempt can inherit the outer loader's ciphertext payloadBytes;
subsequent iterations can supply the local decoded array. This defect limits
claims about successful execution, not the content of the embedded stealer.
The "beacon" function name describes a local process watchdog, not demonstrated
network command-and-control polling.

Stealer behavior verified in IL
Entry method CsvxrnfLmFv sets TLS protocols and installs a certificate callback
that returns true, then calls SY7cB3VQ4. Startup code initializes settings,
checks Sandboxie module presence and WMI virtualization identifiers, and calls
WOMwZkRJxP.CKwdA to collect credentials through 7lTsz3C7.H5y.
Vault extraction calls VaultGetItem_WIN8, obtains pAuthenticatorElement through
marshalling/reflection, and builds credential records. Other recovery routines
read browser/client stores, including Chromium password fields, Outlook profile
passwords, FileZilla and VPN configuration with DPAPI/decrypt helpers.
CKwdA iterates records, calls zEZxYhAZQ to format Host/Username/Password/
Application as HTML, then calls eEbai.J395E1 with that report. J395E1 constructs
FtpWebRequest, sets NetworkCredential and STOR, obtains the request stream and
writes the report's UTF-8 bytes. Both use ftp.hhautoinvestment.co.tz with distinct
accounts. No endpoint connection was attempted during this review.
The configuration enables cookies/contacts collection and selects FTP (LogType
2). EnableKeylogger, EnableScreenLogger, EnableClipboardLogger and AppAddStartup
are false. Hook/screenshot/startup routines exist but enabled surveillance or
startup installation is not established. The executable's version resource
claims Python 3.11.3 (64-bit), although the bytes are a managed stealer; no
Authenticode signature authenticates that claim.

SteamLaundry execution chain
The outer PE is unsigned, declares SteamLaundry in its version resources, and
contains working laundry-themed Windows Forms code. Program.Main constructs
LaundryForm. LaundryForm.InitializeComponent at RVA 0x4250 (IL 0x494 onward)
loads bitmap resource OPlus and passes it to ChannelHarvester with limit 64512.
ChannelHarvester.Materialize traverses columns (x=i/height, y=i%height), appends
RGB bytes and reconstructs an MZ/PE managed assembly. The result reaches
AppDomain.Load through VB LateBinding.LateGet with the concatenated name
"L"+"oad". The code selects GetTypes()[1], then GetMethods()[0], and invokes it
through LateCall, passing decoded resource/key strings and the outer assembly's
name. The ordinary InvokeMember call elsewhere sets Panel.DoubleBuffered; it
is not the payload sink.

The OPlus image is a 147x147 uncompressed BMP. Its first 64512 RGB-column bytes
form a SmartAssembly-obfuscated assembly with namespace HWMonitor and a Sokoban
UI. Its public static Form1.Justy converts the supplied hex strings to LAtK and
wuy, obtains LAtK from the outer resource manager, crops width by 177 and height
by 225 (544x592 becomes 367x367), and reads column-ordered ARGB bytes. The first
four bytes specify a 535041-byte blob. Mist XORs the blob with the trailing-byte
mask (0xa5) and the first three bytes of BigEndianUnicode("wuy"), because the
loop cycles over string.Length rather than the encoded key length. The result
has valid MZ/PE/CLR headers. A proxy-resolved Load invocation loads that assembly,
and GetTypes()[7].GetMethods()[17] is invoked. That assembly contains another
protected resource and dynamically assembled native memory/process API names.
The final protected resource was not fully unpacked; no claim about its network
endpoint, theft routine, or successful injection is made here.

A security engineer would treat automatic hidden assembly execution from the
laundry UI, two pixel concealment layers, reflected dispatch and the supplied
malware-corpus provenance as malicious. These actions do not implement laundry
management or ordinary image rendering. No authorized packaging/deployment
context was supplied; the verdict does not depend on the business-themed name.

Trait corrections
- Add separate notable HTML credential-report labels and FTP STOR/client
  observations, with a hostile source/report/upload profile that requires Vault
  extraction and multiple client stores. The profile states co-occurrence;
  the sample-specific source-to-send flow was established by IL review.
- Stop interpreting the accounting noun Ledger as a hardware wallet. Require
  Ledger Live or the other unambiguous hardware-wallet brands.
- Remove the filename-dependent business-lure-packed-dotnet-resource-payload
  composite. Existing bitmap concealment and module-dispatch rules retain
  independent hostile coverage even when the executable is renamed.
- Remove the generic EnableKeylogger field from MassLogger identity traits;
  use the existing neutral keyboard feature-flag trait in its consumers.
- Remove HTTP-client and renderer-name observations from the count of host
  inventory sources. Those cannot supply independent reconnaissance sources.
- Describe the Sandboxie/WMI finding as probe references rather than a bound
  gate, and require a module-handle lookup reference as well as the target.

Focused checks
Real-payload near misses remove both ASCII/UTF-16 Vault authenticator field
spellings, the STOR command, or the password-report label. Each stops the new
hostile exfiltration profile. Independent FTP/report facts remain where valid.
The original accounting Ledger does not produce a wallet finding; same-length
Trezor and Ledger Live replacements do. A byte-identical ordinary-name.exe
retains both hostile content rules and no filename-based hostile composite.
All three original samples were re-scanned after edits. Each retains at least
two hostile findings in separate objective directories. Verdict markers are
beside the original sample files, not in the traits repository.
